body: I'll take a look and report back when I know more.
FYI: I tried this on the versions mentioned above and can confirm the behavior as stated.
Note that Widget.pluck('DISTINCT name') still works as expected.

I looked at this pluck code - I'm definitely no expert with the rails source, but it seems like pull #8176 did indeed cause this behavior to change, as pluck is now ignoring the select clause and re-building the select_values on the relation based on the parameter(s) to pluck.

However, I don't personally see this as a regression because the previous behavior wasn't actually working in all cases.  As you can see in #7551, if the select had multiple columns, pluck wasn't returning the correct values anyway.  I don't think there's a reliable way for pluck to respect the select clause while also using the parameters passed to pluck.

So yes, there is a behavior change since 3.2.12, but I think that pluck ignoring and rebuilding the select clause is the only way to go.  (Sure we could parse all select_values to see if they have the 'DISTINCT' keyword, but that would be gross and error-prone)

@iancanderson I really like the way you stated your response. Is there any further action that should be taken? Could documentation be improved in any way? Perhaps mentioning in the documentation for `pluck` that "pluck ignores and rebuilds the select clause"?

If the team likes that idea, I can update the docs myself and link back to this issue. Thanks for your input on this!

As previously mentioned using `select` in combination with `pluck` is confusing at best. There are different ways, which are more expressive to reach the same result. None the less it is a change in behaviour, which could break some apps while upgrading. There is no good way to fix this problem other than reverting and on master we keep the patch.

@rafaelfranca @steveklabnik let me know if you want me to revert my changes.
I'll defer to whoever actually knows what the expected behavior should be.

I think the most reasonable solution would be to ignore the `select_values` and replace them with the column passed to pluck. (this is the current implementation on master and 3-2-stable). This behavior is different than 3.2.12 so It could break applications. I think master is fine and on 3-2-stable we could consider a revert. I'm fine either way.

Let's wait for @rafaelfranca
Yeah, I think that's where I'm at, too.
@senny :+1: for keeping this behaviour on master and reverting on 3-2-stable. I'll revert
I'll pull #8176 from the next release candidate, but leave it in 3-2-stable.  Let's see what we can do to be backwards compatible (but maybe issue a warning or something).

issue.title: 3.2.13 regression - pluck is ignoring named scopes
issue.body:
We have a query that looks like:

`Photo.hottest.limit(10).pluck("photos.id")`

Hottest is a named scope, defined as:

```
scope :hottest, lambda { |hotness_period = 24|
  epoch = "2012-04-26 23:36:54 UTC"

  select("photos.*, (LOG(10, count(user_likes.id)) + (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM photos.created_at - to_timestamp('#{epoch}', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'))/#{(hotness_period).hours.to_i})) AS hotness").
    joins("INNER JOIN user_likes ON user_likes.liked_id = photos.id").
    where(:user_likes => {:liked_type => 'Photo'}).
    group(:liked_id, '"photos"."id"').
    order(:hotness).
    reverse_order
}
```

In 3.2.12, the generated query looks like

```
SELECT photos.*, (LOG(10, count(user_likes.id)) + (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM photos.created_at - to_timestamp('2012-04-26 23:36:54 UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'))/86400)) AS hotness, photos.id FROM "photos" INNER JOIN user_likes ON user_likes.liked_id = photos.id WHERE "user_likes"."liked_type" = 'Photo' GROUP BY liked_id, "photos"."id" ORDER BY hotness DESC LIMIT 10
```

while in 3.2.13 it looks like

```
SELECT photos.id FROM "photos" INNER JOIN user_likes ON user_likes.liked_id = photos.id WHERE "user_likes"."liked_type" = 'Photo' GROUP BY liked_id, "photos"."id" ORDER BY hotness DESC LIMIT 10
```

This only happens when using `pluck`. Without it, the query is correct in 3.2.13.

issue.title: Incorrect pluck behaviour when combined with select (rails 4.0)
issue.body:
When combining pluck with select, the generated SQL is not always correct. For instance:

``` ruby
CourseParticipation.select('DISTINCT excel_filename').pluck(:excel_filename)
```

generates a SQL statement without the DISTINCT modifier:

``` sql
SELECT "course_participations"."excel_filename" FROM "course_participations"
```

I'm experiencing this in Rails 4.0. The same code worked perfectly under 3.2.12.

Please note that

``` ruby
CourseParticipation.distinct.pluck(:excel_filename)
```

does produce the expected query (i.e. including DISTINCT).
